quizzes.title: AHDCs, 6th Schedule Councils and Article 371
quizzes.passage:
Ladakh became a Union Territory without a Legislative Assembly in 2019, and this made decentralised local institutions central to its governance. The Ladakh Administration has approved the establishment of Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all seven districts. The step follows an in-principle agreement with the Ministry of Home Affairs to extend constitutional safeguards under Article 371 to the Union Territory.

The Autonomous Hill Development Councils can be compared with the Autonomous District Councils that the Sixth Schedule provides for. The comparison looks at how each body is created, where it applies and what powers it holds, and the two bodies differ on each of these points. Article 371 and Articles 371A to 371J are placed in Part XXI of the Constitution, and together they provide special constitutional safeguards to certain States and regions.

Each article in that group is linked with a particular State or area, so the safeguards do not apply in the same way across the country. The Sixth Schedule councils and the Hill Development Councils therefore rest on different legal foundations, and this difference is central to any comparison of the two. Ladakh has been administered by the Government of India as a Union Territory since 31 October 2019, its capital is Leh, and Kargil serves as the winter capital.

questions.q: Article 370 provides special provisions for which State?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Article 370 among the special provisions for Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed among the aims of Article 371 and Articles 371A to 371J?
options: Grant of financial assistance to special category States
Setting up special economic zones in the northeast
Grant of statehood to Union Territories
questions.explanation: The booklet says these articles aim to protect tribal identity along with culture, customary laws, land rights, local employment and administrative autonomy.

questions.q: Which State is covered by Article 371 along with Gujarat?
questions.explanation: The booklet pairs Article 371 with Maharashtra and Gujarat.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): AHDCs are created through legislation.
Reason (R): AHDCs apply only in Ladakh.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but applying only in Ladakh does not explain how the councils are created.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: I. Article 371A   II. Article 371B   III. Article 371C   IV. Article 371G
List II: A. Mizoram   B. Nagaland   C. Assam   D. Manipur
questions.explanation: Article 371A covers Nagaland, 371B Assam, 371C Manipur and 371G Mizoram.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the councils in Ladakh and under the Sixth Schedule:
I. AHDCs have no judicial authority.
II. 6th Schedule councils have legislative, executive, financial and judicial powers.
III. AHDCs have legislative and judicial powers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: AHDCs have no judicial authority and 6th Schedule councils hold all four kinds of powers, so statement III is wrong.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. 6th Schedule councils can establish village courts under customary tribal laws.
II. AHDCs can establish village courts under customary tribal laws.
III. Article 371 aims to protect land rights.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because only the 6th Schedule councils can set up such courts.

quizzes.title: Ladakh Profile, Demands and the 2025 Regulation
quizzes.passage:
Ladakh is administered by the Government of India as a Union Territory, a status it has held since 31 October 2019. Leh serves as the capital, and Kargil serves as the winter capital. The region shares its borders with Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir, among other neighbours. Ladakh has been in the news because of two recent developments in its governance and public life.

The Centre has introduced a new reservation regulation for the Union Territory. The regulation amends an existing framework as it applies to Ladakh, and it has taken effect after being approved. The rules it sets out apply to the Union Territory alone, which makes the change specific to this region.

The Ladakh Administration has approved the establishment of Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all of its districts. The step follows an in-principle agreement with the Ministry of Home Affairs to extend constitutional safeguards under Article 371 to the Union Territory. Each council will exercise authority over land allotment, district cadre recruitment and promotions, district development planning, and sectors such as health, education, tourism, infrastructure and social welfare.

Decentralised local institutions have become central to governance in Ladakh since it became a Union Territory. Both developments concern how the region is governed, and both are part of the same current affairs story.

questions.q: Which authority approved the Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 for Ladakh?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the President of India approved the regulation.

questions.q: Which areas does the Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 affect?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the regulation affects reservations in government employment and educational admissions.

questions.q: Which demand of the people of Ladakh is linked to representative governance?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists a Legislative Assembly as a demand for representative governance.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The people of Ladakh demand inclusion under the 6th Schedule.
Reason (R): The demand seeks constitutional protection for the region.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the booklet links the 6th Schedule demand to constitutional protection.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: I. Total reservation cap (EWS excluded)   II. Effective date of the regulation   III. Act modified by the regulation   IV. Ladakh's traditional name
List II: A. Maryul   B. 85 per cent   C. 3 June 2025   D. Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, 2004
questions.explanation: The total cap is 85 per cent, the regulation took effect on 3 June 2025, it modifies the 2004 J&K Reservation Act, and the traditional name is Maryul.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ladakh:
I. Ladakh is bordered by Tibet and Xinjiang, which lie in China.
II. India claims Aksai Chin as part of Ladakh, and the region remains under Indian control.
III. Inclusion under the 6th Schedule is one of the demands of the people of Ladakh.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet says Aksai Chin remains under Chinese control.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan) borders Ladakh.
II. The Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 was approved by the Supreme Court.
III. The Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 came into force on 2 June 2025.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the President approved the regulation and it took effect on 3 June 2025.

questions.q: In which year was the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, which the 2025 Regulation modifies, enacted?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, 2004 as the Act modified for Ladakh.

questions.q: What total reservation cap, with EWS quotas excluded, does the 2025 Regulation set? (Give the figure in per cent.)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the regulation raises the total reservation cap to 85 per cent with EWS quotas excluded.

questions.q: From which date was the Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 effective? (Give day, month and year.)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the regulation was effective from 3 June 2025.

questions.q: On which date did the President of India approve the Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025? (Give day, month and year.)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the President approved the regulation on 2 June 2025.

questions.q: What is Ladakh's traditional name, meaning Land of High Passes?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Ladakh as known as the Land of High Passes, or Maryul.

questions.q: Apart from Tibet, which Chinese region borders Ladakh?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Tibet and Xinjiang (China) among the regions bordering Ladakh.

questions.q: Which region administered by Pakistan borders Ladakh?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan) among the regions bordering Ladakh.
